How we pick topics

Every post on this site exists because it won a checklist, not because it was trending on a vibe. Here is the full method, so you can check our work — or copy it.

1. The query has to be winnable

We measure keyword difficulty before we write. Our thresholds: a keyword difficulty (KD) of 10 or less means a new site can realistically rank; KD 10–25 means possible with a clearly better page; KD above 30 is skipped, no matter how tempting the traffic looks. When a tool shows the estimated backlinks needed for the top 10, we record that number too.

2. The SERP decides, not the volume

Volume is the least important signal at launch. What matters is what actually ranks today:

  • Thin SERP (go): forum threads, documentation, or one generic blog — no dedicated, well-crafted page answers the query.
  • Saturated SERP (skip): six or more dedicated comparison articles. Hot-tool "X vs Y" pairs are almost always saturated — that is where content farms pile in.

If a SERP is saturated but our research shows every article misses the actual decision readers face, we may still write — with a clearly differentiated angle, and we will say so.

3. Evidence labels

Every claim carries a source. Numbers we measured ourselves are labeled as ours. Figures we read elsewhere are linked. Contested numbers (like performance benchmarks that change with every release) get described qualitatively instead of copied blindly. We never invent statistics — if we cannot source it, we do not print it.

4. What we refuse to do

  • No affiliate links disguised as verdicts.
  • No mass-generated filler pages.
  • No invented "benchmarks" with unsourced numbers.
  • No rankings promises — we report what the data shows, including when the honest answer is "too early to tell".

5. Corrections

Tools change fast; posts get stale. When we learn a verdict is outdated, we update the post and date the change at the top. Found something wrong? Tell us — that is what the contact page is for.
